statement_summary: Security program covers IT and OT, documented in policies, standards, and the PPCM SSP
Security lead for IT and OT designated in writing
Annual enterprise risk assessment (SP 800-30), and after acquisitions and major changes
Risk acceptance authority by level; no food safety or ammonia safety risk accepted above Low
Quarterly report to the audit committee
One OT change process with HACCP, SSOP, and PSM/RMP review fields
Annual policy and standards review
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions
Vendor security review and contract terms before access; OT vendors through the gateway
Annual reassessment of Tier 1 vendors with SOC 2 review
Annual independent assessment
Acquired sites connect only after the integration standard
Retention of program records (3 years minimum; longer where rules require)
AI systems approved through the AI governance process before use
Unique accounts on every system, including HMIs, SCADA, MES, and the records application
Role-based least privilege; PLC write access only for named engineers
Two-person rule and HMI range limits for formulations, blends, and CCP setpoints
MFA for all accounts, engineering workstations, and all OT remote access
OT remote access only through the gateway; no modems or always-on VPNs
Same-day termination, including OT access and shared password rotation
Remove unneeded access within 5 business days of a transfer
Quarterly access reviews; monthly privileged account review
Password minimums; default passwords changed before connection and checked in CCP verification
IdP lockout; no HMI lockout, compensated by physical protection
Physical access to restricted areas; visitor and contractor escort
Incident response plan and runbooks for ransomware and process tampering
Immediate reporting of suspected incidents and unexplained setpoint or recipe changes
Incident log with discovery time and product-affecting event times
Severity 1 activates the crisis management team within 2 hours
Hold product and review as an unforeseen deviation when CCP control or monitoring is lost
Manual refrigeration operation and PSM/RMP investigation decision when supervisory control is lost
Notifications per the P08 matrix; VP FSQA decides FSIS notification
Insurer hotline before vendors are engaged
Ransom only with CEO, counsel, insurer approval and an OFAC check
Verified restart: logic, recipes, and setpoints match approved versions; FSQA restart checklist
Annual exercise of each runbook with plant leadership
Lessons learned within 30 days, fed to P01, P07, HACCP, and food defense
Data owners classify their data
Restricted data only in approved locations; never on open shares
Encryption at rest and in transit; OT protocols protected by segmentation
Electronic food safety record controls: protected audit trail, authenticated sign-off, synchronized time, locking, separated administration
Records retention (2 years food safety; 6 months SSOP); retrievable within 24 hours
Immutable backups and quarterly restore tests for Restricted and food safety data
Monthly comparison of MES and blend recipes with signed formulation masters
No Restricted or Confidential data in unapproved AI tools
Secure disposal of media and documents
Rules of behavior acknowledged at hire and yearly, including temporaries
Security awareness for all workers, including floor workers and temporaries
Role-based training for controls engineers, MES approvers, and refrigeration operators
No sharing of passwords, badges, or MFA devices
No unapproved devices or USB drives on OT equipment
Approved software only; do not disable security tools
Approved AI tools only; no Restricted data in unapproved tools; human review of consequential output
Mobile devices enrolled in MDM
Report lost devices and suspicious events immediately
